subject: SCR
body: Which Scrum event is a fixed-length event of one month or less that contains all the other events?
explanation: The Sprint: a fixed-length event of one month or less that contains all the other events.

subject: SCR
body: Which Scrum event is the event that lays out the work to be performed for the Sprint?
explanation: Sprint Planning: the event that lays out the work to be performed for the Sprint.

subject: SCR
body: Which Scrum event is a 15-minute event for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal?
explanation: The Daily Scrum: a 15-minute event for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal.

subject: SCR
body: Which Scrum event is the event where the outcome of the Sprint is inspected and future adaptations determined with stakeholders?
explanation: The Sprint Review: the event where the outcome of the Sprint is inspected and future adaptations determined with stakeholders.

subject: SCR
body: Which Scrum event is the event to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness?
explanation: The Sprint Retrospective: the event to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness.

subject: SCR
body: What is the maximum time-box for the Sprint?
explanation: The Sprint is time-boxed to one month or less. Shorter Sprints usually have shorter events.

subject: SCR
body: What is the maximum time-box for Sprint Planning?
explanation: Sprint Planning is time-boxed to 8 hours for a one-month Sprint. Shorter Sprints usually have shorter events.

subject: SCR
body: What is the maximum time-box for the Daily Scrum?
explanation: The Daily Scrum is time-boxed to 15 minutes. Shorter Sprints usually have shorter events.

subject: SCR
body: What is the maximum time-box for the Sprint Review?
explanation: The Sprint Review is time-boxed to 4 hours for a one-month Sprint. Shorter Sprints usually have shorter events.

subject: SCR
body: What is the maximum time-box for the Sprint Retrospective?
explanation: The Sprint Retrospective is time-boxed to 3 hours for a one-month Sprint. Shorter Sprints usually have shorter events.

subject: SCR
body: Which commitment belongs to the Product Backlog?
explanation: Each artifact has a commitment: Product Backlog → Product Goal; Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal; Increment → Definition of Done.

subject: SCR
body: Which commitment belongs to the Sprint Backlog?
explanation: Each artifact has a commitment: Product Backlog → Product Goal; Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal; Increment → Definition of Done.

subject: SCR
body: Which commitment belongs to the Increment?
explanation: Each artifact has a commitment: Product Backlog → Product Goal; Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal; Increment → Definition of Done.

subject: SCR
body: The Product Goal is the commitment for which artifact?
explanation: Product Backlog → Product Goal; Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal; Increment → Definition of Done.

subject: SCR
body: The Sprint Goal is the commitment for which artifact?
explanation: Product Backlog → Product Goal; Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal; Increment → Definition of Done.

subject: SCR
body: The Definition of Done is the commitment for which artifact?
explanation: Product Backlog → Product Goal; Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal; Increment → Definition of Done.

subject: SCR
body: What are the three accountabilities in a Scrum Team?
options: Scrum Master, Team Lead and Developers
Product Owner, Scrum Master and Developers
Project Manager, Product Owner and Testers
explanation: Scrum Guide 2020 defines three accountabilities.

subject: SCR
body: What are the three pillars of empiricism in Scrum?
explanation: Scrum is founded on empiricism and lean thinking.

subject: SCR
body: Which of these is a Scrum value?
explanation: The five values are commitment, focus, openness, respect and courage.

subject: SCR
body: Who is accountable for maximizing the value of the product?
explanation: The Product Owner is one person, not a committee.

subject: SCR
body: Who is accountable for the Scrum Team's effectiveness?
explanation: The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team and the organization.

subject: SCR
body: Who is accountable for creating a plan for the Sprint (the Sprint Backlog)?
explanation: Developers instil quality and adhere to the Definition of Done.

subject: SCR
body: Who can cancel a Sprint?
explanation: A Sprint may be cancelled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

subject: SCR
body: How large is a Scrum Team typically?
explanation: Smaller teams communicate better and are more productive.

subject: SCR
body: Does a Scrum Team have sub-teams or hierarchies?
options: Yes, led by a team lead
No — it is a cohesive unit of professionals focused on one objective
explanation: The Scrum Team is cross-functional and self-managing.

subject: SCR
body: Who must attend the Daily Scrum?
explanation: If the Product Owner or Scrum Master are working on Sprint Backlog items, they participate as Developers.

subject: SCR
body: When multiple Scrum Teams work on the same product, they should have
options: one Product Backlog and one Product Owner
explanation: The product has a single Product Goal and Product Backlog.

subject: SCR
body: What happens to a Product Backlog item that does not meet the Definition of Done at the end of the Sprint?
options: It is counted as half done
It cannot be released or presented at the Sprint Review; it returns to the Product Backlog
explanation: Work must meet the Definition of Done to be part of an Increment.

subject: SCR
body: If the organization has a Definition of Done standard, the Scrum Team must
explanation: If not, the Scrum Team creates one appropriate for the product.

subject: SCR
body: Can an Increment be delivered to stakeholders before the end of the Sprint?
options: No, only at the Sprint Review
explanation: The Sprint Review should never be a gate to releasing value.

subject: SCR
body: What is Product Backlog refinement?
options: The ongoing activity of breaking down and adding detail, such as descriptions, order and size, to Product Backlog items
A formal event time-boxed to 2 hours
explanation: Refinement is ongoing, not a Scrum event.

subject: SCR
body: Which three topics are addressed at Sprint Planning?
options: Why is this Sprint valuable, what can be done, and how will the work get done
explanation: The Sprint Goal is crafted during Sprint Planning.

subject: SCR
body: Can the Sprint Goal change during the Sprint?
options: No — but the Sprint Backlog can be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned
explanation: No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal.

subject: SCR
body: Which event is the last in the Sprint?
explanation: It concludes the Sprint.

subject: SCR
body: The Scrum Guide 2020 describes Scrum Teams as
explanation: They decide internally who does what, when and how.

subject: SCR
body: Scrum is founded on empiricism and
explanation: Lean thinking reduces waste and focuses on essentials.

subject: SCR
body: What is the Product Goal?
options: The long-term objective for the Scrum Team, described in the Product Backlog
explanation: The Scrum Team must fulfil (or abandon) one objective before taking on the next.

subject: SCR
body: Who decides how many Product Backlog items to select for a Sprint?
explanation: The more they know about past performance and capacity, the more confident their forecast.

subject: SCR
body: Is the Sprint Review a formal presentation or approval gate?
options: Yes, it is a status meeting
Yes, the Product Owner signs off
No — it is a working session where the Scrum Team and stakeholders collaborate
explanation: Attendees collaborate on what to do next.

subject: SCR
body: Who participates in the Sprint Retrospective?
explanation: The Scrum Team discusses what went well, problems and solutions.

subject: SCR
body: A new Sprint starts
options: immediately after the conclusion of the previous Sprint
only when the Product Owner approves
at the start of each month
explanation: Sprints are continuous.

subject: SCR
body: The Daily Scrum's structure is decided by
options: the Scrum Guide's fixed three questions
explanation: The Developers can select any structure and techniques that focus on progress toward the Sprint Goal.

subject: SCR
body: What is the pass mark for Scrum.org's PSM I assessment?
explanation: 80 questions in 60 minutes.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: ordering product backlog items?
explanation: Ordering Product Backlog items: the Product Owner.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: clearly expressing product backlog items?
explanation: Clearly expressing Product Backlog items: the Product Owner.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: developing and explicitly communicating the product goal?
explanation: Developing and explicitly communicating the Product Goal: the Product Owner.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: ensuring the product backlog is transparent, visible and understood?
explanation: Ensuring the Product Backlog is transparent, visible and understood: the Product Owner.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: adapting the sprint backlog each day toward the sprint goal?
explanation: Adapting the Sprint Backlog each day toward the Sprint Goal: the Developers.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: instilling quality by adhering to the definition of done?
explanation: Instilling quality by adhering to the Definition of Done: the Developers.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: holding each other accountable as professionals?
explanation: Holding each other accountable as professionals: the Developers.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: sizing product backlog items?
explanation: Sizing Product Backlog items: the Developers.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: causing the removal of impediments to the scrum team's progress?
explanation: Causing the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team's progress: the Scrum Master.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: coaching team members in self-management and cross-functionality?
explanation: Coaching team members in self-management and cross-functionality: the Scrum Master.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: ensuring all scrum events take place and are positive, productive and kept within the time-box?
explanation: Ensuring all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive and kept within the time-box: the Scrum Master.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: leading, training and coaching the organization in its scrum adoption?
explanation: Leading, training and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption: the Scrum Master.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: helping find techniques for effective product goal definition and product backlog management?
explanation: Helping find techniques for effective Product Goal definition and Product Backlog management: the Scrum Master.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: facilitating stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed?
explanation: Facilitating stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed: the Scrum Master.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: creating a usable increment every sprint?
explanation: Creating a usable Increment every Sprint: the Developers.

subject: SCR
body: In Scrum, who is accountable for: deciding whether to cancel a sprint?
explanation: Deciding whether to cancel a Sprint: the Product Owner.

subject: SCR
body: During the Sprint, the Developers realise they cannot finish all the selected work. What should happen?
options: They lower the Definition of Done
The Scrum Master removes items without discussion
They collaborate with the Product Owner to renegotiate the Sprint Backlog scope without endangering the Sprint Goal
explanation: Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned.

subject: SCR
body: A stakeholder asks a Developer directly to add a new feature mid-Sprint. What should the Developer do?
options: Add it to the Sprint Backlog immediately
Ask the Scrum Master to approve it
Refer the request to the Product Owner, who manages the Product Backlog
explanation: Those wanting to change the Product Backlog do so by convincing the Product Owner.

subject: SCR
body: The Sprint Goal has become obsolete because the company changed direction. What may happen?
options: The Scrum Master cancels the Sprint
The Product Owner may cancel the Sprint
The Developers keep working until the end
explanation: Only the Product Owner has authority to cancel a Sprint.

subject: SCR
body: At the Daily Scrum, a long technical discussion starts. What is best?
options: The Scrum Master decides the solution
The relevant Developers continue the discussion after the Daily Scrum
Extend the Daily Scrum to an hour
explanation: Developers often meet immediately afterwards for detailed discussions.

subject: SCR
body: Management wants a report on how the team is progressing. Which is the most transparent source?
options: The Increment and the Sprint Review
A Gantt chart prepared by the Scrum Master
explanation: Scrum relies on transparent artifacts and inspection at the Sprint Review.

subject: SCR
body: The Product Owner is unavailable for most of the Sprint. What is the main risk?
options: The Scrum Master must become Product Owner
Questions about Product Backlog items go unanswered, reducing the value delivered
explanation: The Product Owner's availability supports maximizing value.

subject: SCR
body: A team keeps failing to finish Sprint Backlog items. Where should they discuss how to improve?
options: In a meeting with line management
explanation: The Retrospective identifies the most helpful changes to improve effectiveness.

subject: SCR
body: Two Scrum Teams work on one product. How many Definitions of Done should apply to the Increment?
options: One shared Definition of Done that all teams meet
explanation: Multiple Scrum Teams on a product must mutually define and comply with the same Definition of Done.

subject: SCR
body: Who must be present at Sprint Planning?
explanation: Others may be invited to provide advice.

subject: SCR
body: When is the Sprint Backlog updated?
options: Throughout the Sprint as more is learned
explanation: It is a highly visible, real-time picture of the Developers' work.

subject: SCR
body: What is the main purpose of the Sprint Review?
options: To inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations
To plan the next Daily Scrum
explanation: Progress toward the Product Goal is discussed.

subject: SCR
body: A Developer says they're only a tester and won't write code. According to Scrum, Developers are
options: any members committed to creating any aspect of a usable Increment each Sprint
explanation: Scrum recognises no titles beyond Developer.

subject: SCR
body: What is the Increment?
options: A concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal that is usable and meets the Definition of Done
Everything the team started in the Sprint
explanation: Each Increment is additive to all prior Increments.

subject: SCR
body: How many Increments can be created in a Sprint?
explanation: Multiple Increments may be created within a Sprint.

subject: SCR
body: Is velocity or a burndown chart required by Scrum?
options: Only for Sprints longer than two weeks
No — various practices can forecast progress but they don't replace empiricism
explanation: Scrum doesn't prescribe these techniques.

subject: SCR
body: Which statement about the Scrum Master's role is correct?
options: They are a true leader who serves the Scrum Team and the larger organization
They report individual performance to HR
explanation: Scrum Guide 2020 wording.

subject: SCR
body: What is the purpose of the Sprint Goal?
options: It gives the Developers a single objective for the Sprint, creating coherence and focus
It lists every task in the Sprint
explanation: The Sprint Goal is created during Sprint Planning and added to the Sprint Backlog.

subject: SCR
body: Who creates the Definition of Done if the organization has none?
explanation: It must be appropriate for the product.

subject: SCR
body: Which best describes the Product Backlog?
options: An emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product
explanation: It is the single source of work undertaken by the Scrum Team.

subject: SCR
body: The Sprint Retrospective inspects
options: individuals, interactions, processes, tools and the Definition of Done
explanation: The most impactful improvements may be added to the next Sprint Backlog.

subject: SCR
body: What should the Developers do when work during the Sprint turns out different than expected?
options: Stop and wait for the Sprint Review
Collaborate with the Product Owner on the Sprint Backlog while protecting the Sprint Goal
explanation: Scrum is built on adaptation as soon as possible.

subject: SCR
body: Which Scrum value means the team works on difficult problems and does the right thing?
explanation: Commitment, focus, openness, respect and courage.

subject: SCR
body: Which Scrum value means team members and stakeholders agree to be open about the work and challenges?
explanation: Openness supports transparency.

subject: SCR
body: Why are Sprints limited to one month or less?
options: Longer Sprints can let the Sprint Goal become invalid, increase complexity and increase risk
explanation: Shorter Sprints generate more learning cycles.

subject: SCR
body: What does 'transparency' mean in Scrum?
options: The emergent process and work must be visible to those performing and receiving the work
explanation: Low transparency leads to decisions that diminish value and increase risk.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "The Product Owner can be a committee."
explanation: The Product Owner is one person.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "The Daily Scrum is time-boxed to 15 minutes."
explanation: Regardless of Sprint length.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "The Scrum Master is the manager of the Developers."
explanation: The Scrum Master is a true leader who serves; Scrum Teams are self-managing.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Sprints can be longer than one month."
explanation: Sprints are one month or less.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Every Sprint should have a Sprint Goal."
explanation: It is the commitment for the Sprint Backlog.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Product Backlog refinement is a time-boxed Scrum event."
explanation: It is an ongoing activity, not an event.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Stakeholders are invited to the Sprint Review."
explanation: The Scrum Team presents results to key stakeholders.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Only the Scrum Master can add items to the Sprint Backlog."
explanation: The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Scrum's pillars are transparency, inspection and adaptation."
explanation: These are the three pillars of empiricism.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "The Definition of Done is the commitment for the Increment."
explanation: It creates transparency about what 'done' means.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "The Sprint Review is the last event in the Sprint."
explanation: The Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Scrum Teams are cross-functional."
explanation: Members have all the skills needed to create value each Sprint.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "The Scrum Master can change the Sprint Goal."
explanation: No changes are made that endanger the Sprint Goal.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "The Product Backlog is never complete."
explanation: It is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "The Daily Scrum is only for the Scrum Master to get a status update."
explanation: It is an event for the Developers.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Quality goals should not decrease during the Sprint."
explanation: A Sprint rule from the Scrum Guide.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "A Sprint can have no Sprint Goal if work is unrelated."
explanation: Every Sprint has a Sprint Goal.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Scrum is a lightweight framework."
explanation: It helps people, teams and organizations generate value through adaptive solutions.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "Product Backlog items must be estimated in story points."
explanation: Scrum doesn't prescribe estimation techniques.

subject: SCR
body: TRUE or FALSE? "The Scrum Team is responsible for all product-related activities."
explanation: Including stakeholder collaboration, verification, maintenance, operation, experimentation, R&D.
